title: Digest: The impact of egg and sperm proteins on sea urchin reproductive compatibility
content:
Abstract
Levitan and Hao (2025) investigate reproductive isolation in sea urchins using fertilization assays, pinpointing amino acid substitutions that may cause isolation between species. Genotyping wild urchins showed that a single substitution in an egg protein could limit hybridization where 2 species coexist. Their findings shed light on how interspecific isolation can evolve and manifest in the wild, with eggs potentially under stronger selection to reduce hybridization due to higher costs.
